questions.explanation: When a node goes offline, the remaining nodes keep the network running; upon reconnection, the node catches up by syncing with the rest of the network.
options: The entire network halts until the node comes back online.
The offline node loses its copy of the ledger permanently.
The remaining nodes continue operating and the offline node synchronizes its copy when it reconnects.
All transactions made while the node was offline are lost.
questions.text: If one node in a blockchain network goes offline, what happens?

questions.explanation: False. A majority of nodes will reject an altered local copy, preventing any single person from rewriting past transactions.
questions.text: True or false: A single node can rewrite past transactions on the blockchain and have the change accepted by the network.
